title: CancellationToken is threaded through the whole call chain, never swallowed
statement: A method that accepts a `CancellationToken` passes that same token to every async call it makes; it does not call an inner async method with `default`, `CancellationToken.None`, or no token argument when the inner method offers one.
rationale: A token stops mattering the moment one link in the chain drops it: everything downstream of that call becomes uncancellable even though the outer caller still looks cancellable. `ReviewRunner.PreparePromptAsync` takes one token and threads it into every collection step (sensor evidence, deterministic evidence, subject content) rather than re-deriving or dropping it.

good.caption: One token, threaded through every downstream call.

bad.caption: One of two downstream calls silently drops the caller's token.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, grounded in ReviewRunner.cs's end-to-end token propagation.
